content:
- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast shows a sharp downward move, model tends to undercorrect — actuals often rebound stronger than forecasted.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model overreacts with excessive downward correction — true price often continues upward or stabilizes higher.
- Model consistently underestimates the mean reversion speed — true price often overshoots forecasted low and then rebounds faster than expected.
- In periods of high negative sentiment, model tends to overestimate downward risk and underestimates upward volatility — true price often rises more than forecasted.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward lower prices when sentiment is negative — model fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum or policy surprises.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often underestimates upward momentum — true price frequently rises above forecasted peak.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period, forecast doesn’t adjust until 2–3 days later.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model predicts peak then drops too fast; actuals often plateau or rise again after the drop.
- In high volatility periods, model underweights sentiment impact — true price often reacts more aggressively to sentiment than model suggests.
